senses.gloss: lekha (LP), official letter; cf. likhita, a private letter.
Lekhahāra, Lekhahāraka (EI 21; HD), the carrier of letters (see Rājataraṅgiṇī, VI. 319).

Lekhaka (CII 3, etc.), a writer; a technical term for one who wrote a record [on copper plates, stone slabs, etc., in order to facilitate its correct engraving by an artisan], as opposed to the composer of the document (see also likhita).
 (IE 8-3; EI 28, 30; LL; HD), a writer, scribe or clerk (see Bomb. Gaz., Vol. XVI, pp. 582 and 605; Viṣṇudharmottara, II. 24. 26-28; Śukranītisāra, II. 120).
 (LP), a record or document; mistake for lekhana.
Lekhan-ādhyakṣa (CII 3), the superintendent of the writing of documents.
Lekhayitṛ (EI 12), one who is responsible for getting a grant recorded; mentioned together with Śāsayitṛ; cf. Ājñapti.
Lekhita, Lekhitṛ (EI 24), same as Lekhaka; a writer.
